Proof. Since \( Y = \left( {0,\phi }\right) \) for some function \( \phi \) , we have \( {\nabla }_{Z}Y = \left( {0,{\phi }_{z}}\right)  + \; \Gamma \left( {Z, Y}\right) \) and hence

\[
\left| {\left\langle  {\nabla }_{Z}Y, Z\right\rangle  }_{{h}^{\prime }}\right|  = \left| {\left\langle  {\nabla }_{Z}Y,\left( 1,{f}_{z}\right) \right\rangle  }_{{h}^{\prime }}\right|
\]

\[
\leq  \left| {\left\langle  {f}_{z},{\phi }_{z}\right\rangle  }_{{h}^{\prime }}\right|  + \left| {\left\langle  \Gamma \left( Z, Y\right) , Z\right\rangle  }_{{h}^{\prime }}\right|
\]

\[
\leq  {\left| {f}_{z}\right| }_{{h}^{\prime }}{\left| {\phi }_{z}\right| }_{{h}^{\prime }} + \delta {\left| Z\right| }^{2}\left| Y\right| .
\]

On the other hand \( {\nabla }_{Z}Y = \left( {0,{\phi }_{z}}\right)  + \Gamma \left( {Z, Y}\right) \) so that \( {\left| {\phi }_{z}\right| }_{{h}^{\prime }} \leq  \left| {{\nabla }_{Z}Y}\right|  + \delta \left| Z\right| \left| Y\right| \) . From this the claim follows.

Now for \( \delta  > 0 \) sufficiently small, using the fact that \( 1 - \delta  < {\left| Z\right| }^{2} < \; \left( {1 + \delta }\right) \left( {1.01}\right) \) we can rewrite this as

\[
{Q}_{t} \leq  \frac{{Q}_{zz}}{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}} + \frac{8\left( {1 + {3\delta }}\right) {\left| Y\right| }^{2}\left| {f}_{z}\right| \left| {{\nabla }_{Z}Y}\right| }{{\left( 2 - {\left| Z\right| }^{2}\right) }^{2}} + \frac{4{\left| Y\right| }^{2}\left| {\left( {1 + \delta }\right) \left| {{\nabla }_{Z}Y}\right| \left| {f}_{z}\right| }\right| }{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}\left( {2 - {\left| Z\right| }^{2}}\right) }
\]

\[
- \frac{2{\left| {\nabla }_{Z}Y\right| }^{2}}{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}\left( {2 - {\left| Z\right| }^{2}}\right) } - \frac{\left( {1.95}\right) {\left| Y\right| }^{4}}{{\left( 2 - {\left| Z\right| }^{2}\right) }^{2}} + \widetilde{A}
\]

where \( \widetilde{A} \leq  {C}^{\prime }\left( {{\left| Y\right| }^{2} + \delta \left| Y\right| \left| {{\nabla }_{Z}Y}\right|  + \delta {\left| Y\right| }^{3}}\right) \) . Of course, \( \left| Y\right| \left| {{\nabla }_{Z}Y}\right|  + {\left| Y\right| }^{3} \leq \; 2{\left| Y\right| }^{2} + {\left| {\nabla }_{Z}Y\right| }^{2} + {\left| Y\right| }^{4} \) . Using this, provided that \( \delta \) is sufficiently small, we can rewrite this as

\[
{Q}_{t} \leq  \frac{{Q}_{zz}}{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}} + \frac{1}{\left( 2 - {\left| Z\right| }^{2}\right) } \cdot  \left\lbrack  \frac{8\left( {1 + {3\delta }}\right) \left| {{\nabla }_{Z}Y}\right| \left| {f}_{z}\right| {\left| Y\right| }^{2} - \left( {0.9}\right) {\left| Y\right| }^{4}}{\left( 2 - {\left| Z\right| }^{2}\right) }\right.
\]

\[
+ \frac{4{\left| Y\right| }^{2}\left| {\left( {1 + \delta }\right) \left| {{\nabla }_{Z}Y}\right| \left| {f}_{z}\right|  - \left( {1.9}\right) {\left| {\nabla }_{Z}Y\right| }^{2}}\right| }{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}} - {Q}^{2} + {\widetilde{A}}^{\prime \prime }
\]

where \( {\widetilde{A}}^{\prime \prime } \leq  {C}^{\prime }\left( {\left| Y\right| }^{2}\right) \) . We denote the quantity within the brackets by \( B \) and we estimate

\[
B \leq  8\left( {1 + {3\delta }}\right) \frac{{\left| Y\right| }^{2}\left| {{\nabla }_{Z}Y}\right| \left( {1/{10}}\right) \left( {1 + \delta }\right) }{\left( 2 - \left( {1.01}\right) \left( 1 + \delta \right) \right) } + \frac{4\left( {1/{10}}\right) \left( {1 + \delta }\right) {\left| Y\right| }^{2}\left| {{\nabla }_{Z}Y}\right| }{\left( 1 - \delta \right) }
\]

\[
- \frac{\left( {1.9}\right) }{\left( {1.01}\right) \left( {1 + \delta }\right) }{\left| {\nabla }_{Z}Y\right| }^{2} - \frac{\left( {0.9}\right) {\left| Y\right| }^{4}}{2 - \left( {1.01}\right) \left( {1 + \delta }\right) }
\]

\[
\leq  \left( {1.6}\right) {\left| Y\right| }^{2}\left| {{\nabla }_{Z}Y}\right|  - \left( {0.8}\right) {\left| {\nabla }_{Z}Y\right| }^{2} - \left( {0.8}\right) {\left| Y\right| }^{4}
\]

\[
\leq  0\text{ . }
\]

Therefore,

\[
{Q}_{t} \leq  \frac{{Q}_{zz}}{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}} - {Q}^{2} + \left| \widetilde{A}\right|  \leq  \frac{{Q}_{zz}}{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}} - {\left( Q - {C}_{1}^{\prime }\right) }^{2} + {\left( {C}_{1}^{\prime }\right) }^{2},
\]

for some constant \( {C}_{1}^{\prime } > 1 \) depending only on the curvature bound for the ambient Ricci flow.

Denote by \( l \) the length of \( {I}^{\prime } \) under \( {h}^{\prime } \) . As we have already seen, \( \left( {0.8}\right) r \leq \; l \leq  r \) . We translate the \( z \) -coordinate so that \( z = 0 \) is one endpoint of \( {I}^{\prime } \) and \( z = l \) is the other endpoint; the point \( {x}_{0} \) then corresponds to \( z = l/2 \) . Consider the function \( g = {l}^{2}/\left( {{z}^{2}{\left( l - z\right) }^{2}}\right) \) on \( {I}^{\prime } \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack \) . Direct computation shows that \( {g}_{zz} \leq  {12}{g}^{2} \) . Now set

\[
\widetilde{Q} = Q - {C}_{1}^{\prime }
\]

and

\[
h = \frac{1}{t - {t}^{\prime }} + \frac{4{\left( 1 - \delta \right) }^{-1}{l}^{2}}{{z}^{2}{\left( l - z\right) }^{2}} + {C}_{1}^{\prime }.
\]

Then

\[
- {h}_{t} + {\left( 1 - \delta \right) }^{-1}{h}_{zz} + {\left( {C}_{1}^{\prime }\right) }^{2} \leq  {h}^{2},
\]

so that

\[
{\left( \widetilde{Q} - h\right) }_{t} \leq  \frac{{\widetilde{Q}}_{zz}}{{\left| Z\right| }^{2}} - \frac{{h}_{zz}}{1 - \delta } - {\widetilde{Q}}^{2} + {h}^{2}.
\]

Since both \( h \) and \( {h}_{zz} \) are positive, at any point where \( \widetilde{Q} - h \geq  0 \) and \( {\widetilde{Q}}_{zz} < 0 \) , we have \( {\left( \widetilde{Q} - h\right) }_{t} < 0 \) . At any point where \( {Q}_{zz} \geq  0 \) , using the fact that \( {\left| Z\right| }^{2} \geq  \left( {1 - \delta }\right) \) we have

\[
{\left( \widetilde{Q} - h\right) }_{t} \leq  {\left( 1 - \delta \right) }^{-1}{\left( \widetilde{Q} - h\right) }_{zz} - {\widetilde{Q}}^{2} + {h}^{2}.
\]

Thus, for any fixed \( t \) , at any local maximum for \( \left( {\widetilde{Q} - h}\right) \left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) at which \( \left( {\widetilde{Q} - h}\right) \) is \( \geq  0 \) we have \( {\left( \widetilde{Q} - h\right) }_{t} \leq  0 \) . Since \( \widetilde{Q} - h \) equals \( - \infty \) at the end points of \( {I}^{\prime } \) for all times, there is a continuous function \( f\left( t\right)  = \mathop{\max }\limits_{{z \in  {I}^{\prime }}}\left( {\widetilde{Q} - h}\right) \left( {z, t}\right) \) , defined for all \( t \in  \left( {{t}^{\prime },{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack \) approaching \( - \infty \) uniformly as \( t \) approaches \( {t}^{\prime } \) from above. By the previous discussion, at any point where \( f\left( t\right)  \geq  0 \) we have \( {f}^{\prime }\left( t\right)  \leq  0 \) in the sense of forward difference quotients. It now follows that \( f\left( t\right)  \leq  0 \) for all \( t \in  \left( {{t}^{\prime },{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack \) . This means that for all \( t \in  \left( {{t}^{\prime },{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack \) at the \( {h}^{\prime } \) -midpoint \( {x}_{0} \) of \( {I}^{\prime } \) (the point where \( z = l/2 \) ) we have

\[
Q\left( {{x}_{0}, t}\right)  \leq  \frac{1}{t - {t}^{\prime }} + \frac{{16} \cdot  4{\left( 1 - \delta \right) }^{-1}}{{l}^{2}} + {C}_{1}^{\prime }.
\]

Since \( l \geq  \left( {0.8}\right) r \) and since \( t - {t}^{\prime } \leq  \delta {r}^{2} \) , we see that provided \( \delta \) is sufficiently small (depending on the bound of the curvature of the ambient flow) we have

\[
Q\left( {{x}_{0}, t}\right)  < \frac{3}{2\left( {t - {t}^{\prime }}\right) }
\]

for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack \) . Of course, since \( {\left| Z\right| }^{2} \geq  1 - \delta \) everywhere, this shows that

\[
{k}^{2}\left( {{x}_{0}, t}\right)  \leq  {\left| Y\left( {x}_{0}, t\right) \right| }^{2} = \left( {2 - {\left| Z\left( {x}_{0}, t\right) \right| }^{2}}\right) Q\left( {{x}_{0}, t}\right)  < \frac{2}{\left( t - {t}^{\prime }\right) }
\]

for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack \) . Since \( {x}_{0} \) was an arbitrary point of \( c\left( {\cdot ,{t}^{\prime }}\right) \) , this shows that \( k\left( {x, t}\right)  < \sqrt{\frac{2}{t - {t}^{\prime }}} \) for all \( x \in  c\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) and all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack \) . By the definition of \( {t}_{2} \) this implies that \( {t}_{2} = {t}^{\prime } + \delta {r}^{2} \) and completes the proof of Lemma 19.58.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
(cf. Proposition II.6.3) For any \( A > 0 \) one can find positive constants \( \kappa \left( A\right) ,{K}_{1}\left( A\right) ,{K}_{2}\left( A\right) ,\bar{r}\left( A\right) \) , such that for any \( {t}_{0} < \infty \) there exists \( {\bar{\delta }}_{A}\left( {t}_{0}\right)  > 0 \) , decreasing in \( {t}_{0} \) , with the following property. Suppose that we have a Ricci flow with \( \left( {r,\delta }\right) \) -cutoff on a time interval \( \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) , where \( \delta \left( t\right)  < {\bar{\delta }}_{A}\left( t\right) \) on \( \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0}/2,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) , with normalized initial data. Assume that

1. The solution is unscathed on a parabolic neighborhood \( P\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0},{r}_{0}, - {r}_{0}^{2}}\right) \) , with \( 2{r}_{0}^{2} < {t}_{0} \) .

2. \( \left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right|  \leq  \frac{1}{3}{r}_{0}^{-2} \) on \( P\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0},{r}_{0}, - {r}_{0}^{2}}\right) \) .

3. \( \operatorname{vol}\left( {B\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0},{r}_{0}}\right) }\right)  \geq  {A}^{-1}{r}_{0}^{3} \) .

Then

(a) The solution is \( \kappa \) -noncollapsed on scales less than \( {r}_{0} \) in \( B\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}, A{r}_{0}}\right) \) .

(b) Every point \( x \in  B\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}, A{r}_{0}}\right) \) with \( R\left( {x,{t}_{0}}\right)  \geq  {K}_{1}{r}_{0}^{-2} \) has a canonical neighborhood in the sense of Definition 69.1.

(c) If \( {r}_{0} \leq  \bar{r}\sqrt{{t}_{0}} \) then \( R \leq  {K}_{2}{r}_{0}^{-2} \) in \( B\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}, A{r}_{0}}\right) \) .

The proof of part (a) is analogous to the proof of Theorem 28.2. The proof of part (b) is analogous to the proof of Lemma 53.3. The proof of part (c) is analogous to the proof of Theorem 53.1. We will be brief on the parts of the proof of Proposition 84.1 that are along the same lines as was done before, and will concentrate on the differences.

For part (a), we first remark that the \( \kappa \) -noncollapsing that we want does not follow from the noncollapsing estimate used in the proof of Proposition 77.2, which would give a time-dependent \( \kappa \) . So suppose that \( \left( {x,{t}_{0}}\right)  \in  B\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}, A{r}_{0}}\right) ,\rho  < {r}_{0} \) , the parabolic neighborhood \( P\left( {x,{t}_{0},\rho , - {\rho }^{2}}\right) \) is unscathed and \( \left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right|  \leq  {\rho }^{-2} \) there. We want to get a lower bound on \( {\rho }^{-3}\operatorname{vol}\left( {B\left( {x,{t}_{0},\rho }\right) }\right) \) . We first reduce the case \( \rho  < \frac{r\left( {t}_{0}\right) }{100} \) to the case \( \rho  \geq  \frac{r\left( {t}_{0}\right) }{100} \) .

Suppose that \( \rho  < \frac{r\left( {t}_{0}\right) }{100} \) and let \( s \) be the largest number so that the parabolic neighborhood \( P\left( {x,{t}_{0}, s, - {s}^{2}}\right) \) is unscathed and \( \left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right|  \leq  {s}^{-2} \) there. Clearly \( s \geq  \rho \) . If \( s < \frac{r\left( {t}_{0}\right) }{100} \) then we obtain a lower bound on \( {\rho }^{-3}\operatorname{vol}\left( {B\left( {x,{t}_{0},\rho }\right) }\right) \) as in Sublemma 79.23; a canonical neighborhood of type (d) with small volume cannot occur, in view of condition 3 of Proposition 84.1.

If \( s \geq  \frac{r\left( {t}_{0}\right) }{100} \) and \( \frac{r\left( {t}_{0}\right) }{100} < {r}_{0} \) then once we have proved part (a) of the proposition at scale \( \frac{r\left( {t}_{0}\right) }{100} \) , the Bishop-Gromov inequality will give a lower bound on \( {\rho }^{-3}\operatorname{vol}\left( {B\left( {x,{t}_{0},\rho }\right) }\right) \) and prove part (a) of the proposition at scale \( \rho \) .

Suppose that \( s \geq  \frac{r\left( {t}_{0}\right) }{100} \geq  {r}_{0} \) . Let \( D \) be the largest radius so that \( \left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right|  \leq  {r}_{0}^{-2} \) on \( B\left( {x,{t}_{0}, D}\right) \) . Clearly \( D \geq  s \geq  \rho \) . If \( D \geq  \left( {A + 1}\right) {r}_{0} \) then assumption 3 . of the proposition implies that \( \operatorname{vol}\left( {B\left( {x,{t}_{0},\left( {A + 1}\right) {r}_{0}}\right)  \geq  {A}^{-1}{r}_{0}^{-3}}\right. \) . Since \( \rho  < {r}_{0} \) , the Bishop-Gromov inequality implies a lower bound on \( {\rho }^{-3}\operatorname{vol}\left( {B\left( {x,{t}_{0},\rho }\right) }\right) \) .

Finally, if \( D < \left( {A + 1}\right) {r}_{0} \) then there is some \( {x}_{1} \) with \( {d}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {x,{x}_{1}}\right)  = D \) so that \( \left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {{x}_{1},{t}_{0}}\right) }\right|  = \; {r}_{0}^{-2} \geq  {10000}{\left( r\left( {t}_{0}\right) \right) }^{-2} \) . Slightly moving \( {x}_{1} \) inward toward \( x \) , there is a point \( {x}_{2} \in  B\left( {{x}_{1},{t}_{0}, D - }\right. \; \left. {{cr}\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\right) \) with \( \left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {{x}_{2},{t}_{0}}\right) }\right|  \geq  {5000}{\left( r\left( {t}_{0}\right) \right) }^{-2} \) , for a universal constant \( c \) ; cf. case (b) of the proof of Sublemma 79.23. If \( \bar{r} \) is small then Hamilton-Ivey pinching implies that \( \left( {{x}_{2},{t}_{0}}\right) \) is in a canonical neighborhood, which gives an estimate

(85.2)

\[
\operatorname{vol}\left( {B\left( {x,{t}_{0}, D}\right) }\right)  \geq  \operatorname{vol}\left( {B\left( {{x}_{2},{t}_{0},\operatorname{cr}\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\right) }\right)  \geq  \text{ const. }{\left( r\left( {t}_{0}\right) \right) }^{3} \geq  {10}^{6}\text{ const. }{r}_{0}^{3}.
\]

Since \( \rho  \leq  D \) , the Bishop-Gromov inequality now implies a lower bound on \( {\rho }^{-3}\operatorname{vol}\left( {B\left( {x,{t}_{0},\rho }\right) }\right) \) , depending on \( A \) .

This shows that it suffices to consider scales \( \rho \) that are at least \( r\left( {t}_{0}\right) /{100} \) . To continue, we recall the idea of the proof of Theorem 28.2. With the notation of Theorem 28.2, after rescaling so that \( {r}_{0} = {t}_{0} = 1 \) , we had a point \( x \in  B\left( {{x}_{0},1, A}\right) \) around which we wanted to prove noncollapsing. Defining \( l \) using curves starting at \( \left( {x,1}\right) \) , we wanted to find a point \( \left( {y,1/2}\right)  \in  B\left( {{x}_{0},1/2,1/2}\right) \) so that \( l\left( {y,1/2}\right) \) was bounded above by a universal constant. Given such a point, we concatenated a minimizing \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic (from \( \left( {x,1}\right) \) to \( \left( {y,1/2}\right) \) ) with curves emanating backward in time from \( \left( {y,1/2}\right) \) . Then the bounded geometry near \( \left( {y,1/2}\right) \) allowed us to estimate from below the reduced volume at a time slightly less than \( 1/2 \) .

We knew that there was some point \( y \in  M \) so that \( l\left( {y,1/2}\right)  \leq  \frac{3}{2} \) , but the issue in Theorem 28.2 was to find a point \( \left( {y,1/2}\right)  \in  B\left( {{x}_{0},1/2,1/2}\right) \) with \( l\left( {y,1/2}\right) \) bounded above by a universal constant. The idea was to take the proof that some point \( y \in  M \) has \( l\left( {y,1/2}\right)  \leq  \frac{3}{2} \) and localize it near \( {x}_{0} \) . The proof of Theorem 28.2 used the function \( h\left( {y, t}\right)  = \; \phi \left( {d\left( {y, t}\right)  - A\left( {{2t} - 1}\right) }\right) \left( {\bar{L}\left( {y,1 - t}\right)  + 7}\right) \) . Here \( \phi \) was a certain nondecreasing function that is one on \( \left( {-\infty ,1/{20}}\right) \) and infinite on \( \lbrack 1/{10},\infty ) \) , and \( \bar{L}\left( {q,\tau }\right)  = 2\sqrt{\tau }L\left( {q,\tau }\right) \) . Clearly min \( h\left( {\cdot ,1}\right)  \leq  7 \) and \( \min h\left( {\cdot ,1/2}\right) \) is achieved in \( B\left( {{x}_{0},1/2,1/{10}}\right) \) . The equation \( \square h \geq   - \left( {6 + C\left( A\right) }\right) h \) implied that \( \frac{d}{dt}\min h \geq   - \left( {6 + C\left( A\right) }\right) \min h \) , and \( \operatorname{so}\left( {\min h}\right) \left( t\right)  \leq  7{e}^{\left( {6 + C\left( A\right) }\right) \left( {1 - t}\right) } \) .

In the present case, if one knew that the possible contribution of a barely admissible curve to \( h\left( {y, t}\right) \) was greater than \( 7{e}^{\left( {6 + C\left( A\right) }\right) \left( {1 - t}\right) } + \epsilon \) then one could still apply the maximum principle to find a point \( \left( {y,1/2}\right) \) with \( h\left( {y,1/2}\right)  \leq  7{e}^{\left( {6 + C\left( A\right) }\right) /2} \) . For this, it suffices to know that the possible contribution of a barely admissible curve to \( \bar{L}\left( {q,\tau }\right) \) can be bounded below by a sufficiently large number. However, Lemma 79.3 only says that we can make the contribution of a barely admissible curve to \( L \) large (using the lower scalar curvature bound to pass from \( {\mathcal{L}}_{ + } \) to \( \mathcal{L} \) ). Because of the factor \( 2\sqrt{\tau } \) in the definition of \( \bar{L}\left( {q,\tau }\right) \) , we cannot necessarily say that its contribution to \( \bar{L}\left( {q,\tau }\right) \) is large. To salvage the argument, the idea is to redefine \( h \) and redo the proof of Theorem 28.2 in order to get an extra factor of \( \sqrt{\tau } \) in \( \min h \) .

(The use of Lemma 79.3 is similar to what was done in the proof of Proposition 77.2. However, there is a difference in scales. In Proposition 77.2 one was working at a microscopic scale in order to construct the Ricci flow with surgery. The function \( \bar{\delta }\left( t\right) \) in Proposition 77.2 was relevant to this scale. In the present case we are working at the macroscopic scale \( {r}_{0} \sim  \sqrt{{t}_{0}} \) in order to analyze the long-time behavior of the Ricci flow with surgery. The function \( {\delta }_{A}\left( t\right) \) of Proposition 84.1 is relevant to this scale. Thus we will end up further reducing the surgery function \( \bar{\delta }\left( t\right) \) of Proposition 77.2 in order to be able to apply Proposition 84.1.)

By assumption, \( \left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right|  \leq  1 \) at \( t = 0 \) . From Lemma 79.11, \( R \geq   - \frac{3}{2}\frac{1}{t + 1/4} \) . Then for \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0} - {r}_{0}^{2}/2,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack  , \)

(85.3)

\[
R{r}_{0}^{2} \geq   - \frac{3}{2}\frac{{r}_{0}^{2}}{{t}_{0} - {r}_{0}^{2}/2} \geq   - \frac{3}{2}\frac{{r}_{0}^{2}}{2{r}_{0}^{2} - {r}_{0}^{2}/2} =  - 1.
\]

After rescaling so that \( {r}_{0} = 1 \) , the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0} - {r}_{0}^{2},{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) is shifted to \( \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) . Then for \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {\frac{1}{2},1}\right\rbrack \) , we certainly have \( R \geq   - 3 \) .

From this, if \( 0 < \tau  \leq  \frac{1}{2} \) then \( \bar{L}\left( {y,\tau }\right)  \geq   - 6\sqrt{\tau }{\int }_{0}^{\tau }\sqrt{v}{dv} =  - 4{\tau }^{2} \) , so \( \widehat{L}\left( {y,\tau }\right)  \equiv \; \bar{L}\left( {y,\tau }\right)  + 2\sqrt{\tau } > 0. \)

Putting

(85.4)

\[
h\left( {y,\tau }\right)  = \phi \left( {{d}_{t}\left( {{x}_{0}, y}\right)  - A\left( {{2t} - 1}\right) }\right) \widehat{L}\left( {y,\tau }\right)
\]

and using the fact that \( \frac{d}{dt}\sqrt{\tau } =  - \frac{d}{d\tau }\sqrt{\tau } =  - \frac{1}{2\sqrt{\tau }} \) , the computations of the proof of Theorem 28.2 give

(85.5)

\[
\square h \geq   - \left( {\bar{L} + 2\sqrt{\tau }}\right) C\left( A\right) \phi  - {6\phi } - \frac{1}{\sqrt{\tau }}\phi
\]

\[
=  - C\left( A\right) h - \left( {6 + \frac{1}{\sqrt{\tau }}}\right) \phi .
\]

Then if \( {h}_{0}\left( \tau \right)  = \min h\left( {\cdot ,\tau }\right) \) , we have

(85.6)

\[
\frac{d}{d\tau }\left( {\log \left( \frac{{h}_{0}\left( \tau \right) }{\sqrt{\tau }}\right) }\right)  = {h}_{0}^{-1}\frac{d{h}_{0}}{d\tau } - \frac{1}{2\tau } \leq  C\left( A\right)  + \left( {6 + \frac{1}{\sqrt{\tau }}}\right) \frac{\phi }{{h}_{0}} - \frac{1}{2\tau }
\]

\[
= C\left( A\right)  + \left( {6 + \frac{1}{\sqrt{\tau }}}\right) \frac{1}{\bar{L} + 2\sqrt{\tau }} - \frac{1}{2\tau }
\]

\[
= C\left( A\right)  + \frac{6\sqrt{\tau } + 1}{\sqrt{\tau L} + {2\tau }} - \frac{1}{2\tau }.
\]

As \( \bar{L} \geq   - 4{\tau }^{2} \) ,

(85.7)

\[
\frac{d}{d\tau }\left( {\log \left( \frac{{h}_{0}\left( \tau \right) }{\sqrt{\tau }}\right) }\right)  \leq  C\left( A\right)  + \frac{6\sqrt{\tau } + 1}{{2\tau } - 4{\tau }^{2}\sqrt{\tau }} - \frac{1}{2\tau } \leq  C\left( A\right)  + \frac{50}{\sqrt{\tau }}.
\]

As \( \tau  \rightarrow  0 \) , the Euclidean space computation gives \( \bar{L}\left( {q,\tau }\right)  \sim  {\left| q\right| }^{2} \) , so \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  0}}\frac{{h}_{0}\left( \tau \right) }{\sqrt{\tau }} = 2 \) . Then

(85.8)

\[
{h}_{0}\left( \tau \right)  \leq  2\sqrt{\tau }\exp \left( {C\left( A\right) \tau  + {100}\sqrt{\tau }}\right) .
\]

This estimate has the desired extra factor of \( \sqrt{\tau } \) .

It now suffices to show that for a barely admissible curve \( \gamma \) that hits a surgery region at time \( 1 - \tau \) ,

(85.9)

\[
{\int }_{0}^{\tau }\sqrt{v}\left( {R\left( {\gamma \left( {1 - v}\right) , v}\right)  + {\left| \dot{\gamma }\left( v\right) \right| }^{2}}\right) {dv} \geq  \exp \left( {C\left( A\right) \tau  + {100}\sqrt{\tau }}\right)  + \epsilon ,
\]

where \( 0 < \tau  \leq  \frac{1}{2} \) . Choosing \( {\bar{\delta }}_{A}\left( {t}_{0}\right) \) small enough, this follows from Lemma 79.3 along with the lower scalar curvature bound. Then we can apply the maximum principle and follow the proof of Theorem 28.2. In our case the bounded geometry near \( \left( {y,1/2}\right)  \in  B\left( {{x}_{0},1/2,1/2}\right) \) comes from assumptions 2 and 3 of the Proposition. The function \( {\bar{\delta }}_{A} \) is now determined. After reintroducing the scale \( {r}_{0} \) , this proves part (a) of the proposition.

The proof of part (b) is similar to the proofs of Lemma 53.3 and Proposition 77.2. Suppose that for some \( A > 0 \) the claim is not true. Then there is a sequence of Ricci flows \( {\mathcal{M}}^{\alpha } \) which together provide a counterexample. In particular, some point \( \left( {{x}^{\alpha },{t}^{\alpha }}\right)  \in  B\left( {{x}_{0}^{\alpha },{t}_{0}^{\alpha }, A{r}_{0}^{\alpha }}\right) \) has \( R\left( {{x}^{\alpha },{t}^{\alpha }}\right)  \geq  {K}_{1}^{\alpha }{\left( {r}_{0}^{\alpha }\right) }^{-2} \) but does not have a canonical neighborhood, where \( {K}_{1}^{\alpha } \rightarrow  \infty \) as \( \alpha  \rightarrow \; \infty \) . Because of the canonical neighborhood assumption, we must have \( {K}_{1}^{\alpha }{\left( {r}_{0}^{\alpha }\right) }^{-2} \leq  r{\left( {t}_{0}^{\alpha }\right) }^{-2} \) . Then \( 2{K}_{1}^{\alpha } \leq  {K}_{1}^{\alpha }{t}_{0}^{\alpha }{\left( {r}_{0}^{\alpha }\right) }^{-2} \leq  {t}_{0}^{\alpha }r{\left( {t}_{0}^{\alpha }\right) }^{-2} \) . Since \( {K}_{1}^{\alpha } \rightarrow  \infty \) and the function \( t \rightarrow  \operatorname{tr}{\left( t\right) }^{-2} \) is bounded on any finite \( t \) -interval, it follows that \( {t}_{0}^{\alpha } \rightarrow  \infty \) . Applying point selection to each \( {\mathcal{M}}^{\alpha } \) and removing the superscripts, there are points \( \bar{x} \in  B\left( {{x}_{0},\bar{t},{2A}{r}_{0}}\right) \) with \( \bar{t} \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0} - {r}_{0}^{2}/2,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) such that \( \bar{Q} \equiv  R\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right)  \geq  {K}_{1}{r}_{0}^{-2} \) and \( \left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right) \) does not have a canonical neighborhood, but each point \( \left( {x, t}\right)  \in  \bar{P} \) with \( R\left( {x, t}\right)  \geq  4\bar{Q} \) does have a canonical neighborhood, where \( \bar{P} = \left\{  {\left( {x, t}\right)  : {d}_{t}\left( {{x}_{0}, x}\right)  \leq  {d}_{\bar{t}}\left( {{x}_{0},\bar{x}}\right)  + {K}_{1}^{1/2}{\bar{Q}}^{-1/2}, t \in  \left\lbrack  {\bar{t} - \frac{1}{4}{K}_{1}{\bar{Q}}^{-1},\bar{t}}\right\rbrack  }\right\} \) . From (a), we have noncollapsing in \( \bar{P} \) . Rescaling by \( {\bar{Q}}^{-1} \) , we have bounded curvature at bounded distances from \( \bar{x} \) ; see Lemma 70.2. Then we can extract a pointed limit \( {X}_{\infty } \) , which we think of as a time zero slice, that will have nonnegative sectional curvature. (The required pinching for the last statement comes from the assumption that \( 2{r}_{0}^{2} < {t}_{0} \) , along with the fact that \( {K}_{1}^{\alpha } \rightarrow  \infty \) .) The fact that points \( \left( {x, t}\right)  \in  \bar{P} \) with \( R\left( {x, t}\right)  \geq  4\bar{Q} \) have a canonical neighborhood implies that regions of large scalar curvature in \( {X}_{\infty } \) have canonical neighborhoods, from which one can deduce as in Section 46 that the sectional curvatures of \( {X}_{\infty } \) are globally bounded above by some \( {Q}_{0} > 0 \) . Then for each \( \bar{A} \) , Lemmas 27.8 and 70.1 imply that for large \( \alpha \) , the parabolic neighborhood \( P\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t},\bar{A}{\bar{Q}}^{-1/2}, - \epsilon {\eta }^{-1}{Q}_{0}^{-1}{\bar{Q}}^{-1}}\right) \) is contained in \( \bar{P} \) . (Here \( \epsilon \) is a small parameter, which we absorb in the global parameter \( \epsilon \) .) In applying Lemma 27.8 we use the curvature bound near \( {x}_{0} \) coming from the hypothesis of the proposition along with the curvature bound near \( \bar{x} \) just derived; cf. the proof of Lemma 53.3. In addition, we claim that \( P\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t},\bar{A}{\bar{Q}}^{-1/2}, - \epsilon {\eta }^{-1}{Q}_{0}^{-1}{\bar{Q}}^{-1}}\right) \) is unscathed. This is proved as in Section 80. Recall that the idea is to show that a surgery in \( P\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t},\bar{A}{\bar{Q}}^{-1/2}, - \epsilon {\eta }^{-1}{Q}_{0}^{-1}{\bar{Q}}^{-1}}\right) \) implies that \( \left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right) \) lies in a canonical neighborhood, which contradicts our assumption. In the argument we use the fact that \( {t}_{0}^{\alpha } \rightarrow  \infty \) implies \( \delta \left( {t}_{0}^{\alpha }\right)  \rightarrow  0 \) in order to rule out surgeries; this is the replacement for the condition \( {\bar{\delta }}^{\alpha } \rightarrow  0 \) that was used in Section 80.

We extend \( {X}_{\infty } \) to the maximal backward-time limit and obtain an ancient \( \kappa \) -solution, which contradicts the assumption that the points \( \left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right) \) did not have canonical neighborhoods. This proves part (b) of the proposition.

To prove part (c), we can rescale \( {t}_{0} \) to 1 and then apply Lemma 70.2; see the end of the proof of Theorem 53.1. The \( \Phi \) -pinching that we use comes from the Hamilton-Ivey estimate of (B.4). We recall that in the proof of Theorem 53.1 we need to get nonnegative curvature in the region \( W \) near the blowup point; this comes from the fact that \( {\bar{r}}^{\alpha } \rightarrow  0 \) in the contradiction argument, along with the Hamilton-Ivey pinching.

This proves the proposition.

(Noncollapsing estimate) (cf. Lemma II.5.2)

Suppose \( \epsilon  \geq  {r}_{ - } \geq  {r}_{ + } > 0,{\kappa }_{ - } > 0,{E}_{ - } > 0 \) and \( E < \infty \) . Then there are constants \( \bar{\delta } = \bar{\delta }\left( {{r}_{ - },{r}_{ + },{\kappa }_{ - },{E}_{ - }, E}\right) \) and \( {\kappa }_{ + } = {\kappa }_{ + }\left( {{r}_{ - },{\kappa }_{ - },{E}_{ - }, E}\right) \) with the following property. Suppose that

- \( a < b < c,\;b - a \geq  {E}_{ - },\;c - a \leq  E, \)

- \( \mathcal{M} \) is a Ricci flow with \( \left( {r,\delta }\right) \) -cutoff with normalized initial condition defined on a time interval containing \( \lbrack a, c) \) ,

- \( r \geq  {r}_{ - } \) on \( \lbrack a, b) \) and \( r \geq  {r}_{ + } \) on \( \lbrack b, c) \) ,

- \( r \leq  \epsilon \) ,

- \( \mathcal{M} \) is \( {\kappa }_{ - } \) -noncollapsed at scales below \( \epsilon \) on \( \lbrack a, b) \) and

- \( \delta  \leq  \bar{\delta } \) on \( \lbrack a, c) \) ,

Then \( \mathcal{M} \) is \( {\kappa }_{ + } \) -noncollapsed at scales below \( \epsilon \) on \( \lbrack b, c) \) .

Proof. In the proof, we can assume that \( \frac{{r}_{ + }}{100} \leq  \sqrt{{E}_{ - }/3} \) . If this were not the case then we could prove the lemma with \( {r}_{ + } \) replaced by \( {100}\sqrt{{E}_{ - }/3} \) . Then the lemma would also hold for the original value of \( {r}_{ + } \) .

First, from Lemma 79.11, \( R \geq   - 6 \) on \( {\mathcal{M}}_{\lbrack a, c)} \) .

Suppose that \( {r}_{0} \in  \left( {0,\epsilon }\right) ,\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  \in  {\mathcal{M}}_{\lbrack b, c)}, B\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0},{r}_{0}}\right) \) is a proper ball unscathed on the interval \( \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0} - {r}_{0}^{2},{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) , and \( \left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right|  \leq  {r}_{0}^{-2} \) on \( P\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0},{r}_{0}, - {r}_{0}^{2}}\right) \) .

We first assume that \( {r}_{0} \leq  \sqrt{{E}_{ - }/3} \) and \( {r}_{0} \geq  \frac{{r}_{ + }}{100} \) .

We will consider \( \mathcal{L} \) -length, \( {\mathcal{L}}_{ + } \) -length, etc in \( {\mathcal{M}}_{\left\lbrack  a,{t}_{0}\right) } \) with basepoint at \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) . Suppose that \( \widehat{t} \in  \left\lbrack  {a,{t}_{0}}\right) \) . Then for any admissible curve \( \gamma  : \left\lbrack  {\widehat{t},{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  {\mathcal{M}}_{\left\lbrack  a,{t}_{0}\right\rbrack  } \) ending at \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) , we have

(79.14)

\[
\mathcal{L}\left( \gamma \right)  \leq  {\mathcal{L}}_{ + }\left( \gamma \right)  \leq  \mathcal{L}\left( \gamma \right)  + {\int }_{a}^{c}6\sqrt{c - t}{dt} \leq  \mathcal{L}\left( \gamma \right)  + 4{E}^{\frac{3}{2}}
\]

\[
\text{ and }l\left( {x, t}\right)  \geq  \frac{{L}_{ + } - 4{E}^{\frac{3}{2}}}{2{E}^{\frac{1}{2}}}\text{ . }
\]

Assume that \( \bar{\delta } \leq  {F}_{0}\left( {4{E}^{\frac{1}{2}} + 4{E}^{\frac{3}{2}},\frac{{r}_{ + }}{100},{r}_{ + }}\right) \) where \( {F}_{0} \) is the function from Lemma 79.3. Then by (79.14) and Lemma 79.3, we conclude that any admissible curve \( \left\lbrack  {\widehat{t},{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  {\mathcal{M}}_{\left\lbrack  a,{t}_{0}\right\rbrack  } \) ending at \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) which does not lie in \( {\mathcal{M}}_{\text{ reg }} \cup  {\mathcal{M}}_{{t}_{0}} \) has reduced length bounded below by \( 2 = \frac{3}{2} + \frac{1}{2} \) . By Lemma 78.6 there is an admissible curve \( \gamma  : \left\lbrack  {a,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \mathcal{M} \) ending at \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) such that

(79.15)

\[
\mathcal{L}\left( \gamma \right)  = L\left( {\gamma \left( a\right) }\right)  = 2\sqrt{{t}_{0} - a}l\left( {\gamma \left( a\right) }\right)  \leq  3\sqrt{{t}_{0} - a},
\]

so by (79.14) it follows that

(79.16)

\[
{\mathcal{L}}_{ + }\left( \gamma \right)  \leq  3\sqrt{{t}_{0} - a} + 4{E}^{\frac{3}{2}} \leq  3\sqrt{E} + 4{E}^{\frac{3}{2}}.
\]

Set

(79.17)

\[
{t}_{1} = a + \frac{b - a}{3},\;{t}_{2} = a + \frac{2\left( {b - a}\right) }{3}
\]

and

(79.18)

\[
\rho  = \left( {3\sqrt{E} + 4{E}^{\frac{3}{2}}}\right) {\left( \frac{1}{3}{E}_{ - }\right) }^{-\frac{3}{2}}.
\]

By construction, \( {t}_{2} \leq  {t}_{0} - {r}_{0}^{2} \) . Note that there is a \( \bar{t} \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{1},{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack \) such that \( R\left( {\gamma \left( \bar{t}\right) }\right)  \leq  \rho \) . Otherwise we would get

(79.19)

\[
{\mathcal{L}}_{ + }\left( \gamma \right)  > {\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{t}_{0} - t}{R}_{ + }\left( {\gamma \left( t\right) }\right) {dt} \geq  \sqrt{\frac{1}{3}{E}_{ - }}{\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}{\rho dt} \geq  \sqrt{\frac{1}{3}{E}_{ - }}\left( {\frac{1}{3}{E}_{ - }}\right) \rho  = 3\sqrt{E} + 4{E}^{\frac{3}{2}},
\]

contradicting (79.16).

Put \( \bar{x} = \gamma \left( \bar{t}\right) \) . By Lemma 70.1, there is an estimate of the form

(79.20)

\[
R \leq  \text{ const. }{s}^{-2}
\]

on the parabolic ball \( \widehat{P} = P\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}, s, - {s}^{2}}\right) \) with \( {s}^{-2} = \) const. \( \left( {\rho  + {r}_{ - }^{-2}}\right) \) . Appealing to Hamilton-Ivey curvature pinching as usual, we get that \( \left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right|  \leq \) const. \( {s}^{-2} \) in \( \widehat{P} \) . If \( \bar{t} - {s}^{2} < a \) then we shrink \( s \) (as little as possible) to ensure that \( \widehat{P} \subset  {\mathcal{M}}_{\lbrack a, b)} \) . Provided that \( \bar{\delta } \) is less than a small constant \( {c}_{1} = {c}_{1}\left( {{r}_{ - },{E}_{ - }, E}\right) \) , we can guarantee that \( \widehat{P} \) is unscathed, by forcing the curvature in a surgery cap to exceed our bound (79.20) on \( R \) . Put \( U = {\mathcal{M}}_{\bar{t} - \frac{1}{2}{s}^{2}} \cap  \widehat{P} \) . If \( s < \epsilon \) then the \( {\kappa }_{ - } \) -noncollapsing assumption on \( \lbrack a, b) \) gives a lower bound on \( \operatorname{vol}\left( {\widetilde{B}\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}, s}\right) }\right) {s}^{-3} \) . If \( s \geq  \epsilon \) then the \( {\kappa }_{ - } \) -noncollapsing assumption gives a lower bound on \( \operatorname{vol}\left( {B\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t},\epsilon /2}\right) }\right) {\left( \epsilon /2\right) }^{-3} \) . In either, case, we get a lower bound on \( \operatorname{vol}\left( {B\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}, s}\right) }\right) \) and hence a lower bound \( \operatorname{vol}\left( U\right)  \geq \; v = v\left( {{r}_{ - },{\kappa }_{ - },{E}_{ - }, E}\right) \) . Now every point in \( U \) can be joined to \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) by a curve of \( {\mathcal{L}}_{ + } \) - length at most \( {\Lambda }_{ + } = {\Lambda }_{ + }\left( {{r}_{ - },{E}_{ - }, E}\right) \) , by concatenating an admissible curve \( \left\lbrack  {\bar{t} - \frac{1}{2}{s}^{2},\bar{t}}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \mathcal{M} \) (of controlled \( {\mathcal{L}}_{ + } \) -length) with \( {\left. \gamma \right| }_{\left\lbrack  \bar{t},{t}_{0}\right\rbrack  } \) . Shrinking \( \bar{\delta } \) again, we can apply Lemmas 78.3 and 79.3 with (79.14) to ensure that every point in \( U \) can be joined to \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) by a minimizing \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic lying in \( {\mathcal{M}}_{\text{ reg }} \cup  {\mathcal{M}}_{{t}_{0}} \) . Lemma 78.11 then implies that

(79.21)

\[
\operatorname{vol}\left( {B\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0},{r}_{0}}\right) }\right) {r}_{0}^{-3} \geq  {\kappa }_{1} = {\kappa }_{1}\left( {{r}_{ - },{\kappa }_{ - },{E}_{ - }, E}\right) .
\]

(We briefly recall the argument. We have a parabolic ball around \( \left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right) \) , of small but controlled size, on which we have uniform curvature bounds. The lower volume bound coming from the \( {\kappa }_{ - } \) -noncollapsing assumption on \( \lbrack a, b) \) means that we have bounded geometry on the parabolic ball. As we have a fixed upper bound on \( l\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right) \) , we can estimate from below the reduced volume of the accessible points \( Y \subset  {\mathcal{M}}_{\bar{t} - \frac{1}{2}{s}^{2}}^{ + } \) . Then we obtain a lower bound on \( \operatorname{vol}\left( {B\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0},{r}_{0}}\right) }\right) {r}_{0}^{-3} \) as in Theorem 26.2.)

This completes the proof of the lemma when \( {r}_{0} \leq  \sqrt{{E}_{ - }/3} \) and \( {r}_{0} \geq  \frac{{r}_{ + }}{100} \) .

(79.22)

Now suppose that \( {r}_{0} > \sqrt{{E}_{ - }/3} \) . Applying our noncollapsing estimate (79.21) to the ball of radius \( \sqrt{{E}_{ - }/3} \) gives

\[
\operatorname{vol}\left( {B\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0},{r}_{0}}\right) }\right) {r}_{0}^{-3} \geq  \left( {\operatorname{vol}\left( {B\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0},\sqrt{{E}_{ - }/3}}\right) {\left( {E}_{ - }/3\right) }^{-\frac{3}{2}}}\right) }\right) \frac{{\left( {E}_{ - }/3\right) }^{\frac{3}{2}}}{{r}_{0}^{3}} \geq  {\kappa }_{1}\frac{{\left( {E}_{ - }/3\right) }^{\frac{3}{2}}}{{\epsilon }^{3}} = {\kappa }_{2},
\]

where \( {\kappa }_{2} = {\kappa }_{2}\left( {{r}_{ - },{\kappa }_{ - },{E}_{ - }, E}\right) \) .

The next sublemma deals with the case when \( {r}_{0} < \frac{{r}_{ + }}{100} \) .

Sublemma 79.23. If \( {r}_{0} < \frac{{r}_{ + }}{100} \) then \( \operatorname{vol}\left( {B\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0},{r}_{0}}\right) }\right) {r}_{0}^{-3} \geq  {\kappa }_{3} = {\kappa }_{3}\left( {{r}_{ - },{\kappa }_{ - },{E}_{ - }, E}\right) \) .

Proof. Let \( s \) be the maximum of the numbers \( \bar{s} \in  \left\lbrack  {{r}_{0},\frac{{r}_{ + }}{100}}\right\rbrack \) such that \( B\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0},\bar{s}}\right) \) is unscathed on \( \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0} - {\bar{s}}^{2},{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) , and \( \left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right|  \leq  {\bar{s}}^{-2} \) on \( P\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0},\bar{s}, - {\bar{s}}^{-2}}\right) \) . Then either

(a) Some point \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) on the frontier of \( P\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}, s, - {s}^{2}}\right) \) lies in a surgery cap

or

(b) Some point \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) in the closure of \( P\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}, s, - {s}^{2}}\right) \) has \( \left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right|  = {s}^{-2} \)

or

(c) \( s = \frac{{r}_{ + }}{100} \) .

In case (a) the scalar curvature at \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) will satisfy \( R\left( {x, t}\right)  \in  \left( {\frac{{h}^{-2}}{2},{10}{h}^{-2}}\right) \) , since \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) lies in the cap at the surgery time. Since \( \left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  {s}^{-2} \) we conclude that \( s \leq \) const. \( h\left( t\right) \) . If \( \bar{\delta } \) is small then the pointed time slice \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}_{t},\left( {x, t}\right) }\right) \) will be close, modulo scaling by \( h\left( t\right) \) , to the initial condition of the standard solution with the basepoint somewhere in the cap. Using the fact that the time slices of \( P\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}, s, - {s}^{2}}\right) \) have comparable metrics, along with the fact that \( {r}_{0} \leq  s \leq \) const. \( h\left( t\right) \) , we get a lower bound vol \( \left( {B\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0},{r}_{0}}\right) }\right) {r}_{0}^{-3} \geq \) const.

In case (b), we have a static curve \( \gamma  : \left\lbrack  {t,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \mathcal{M} \) such that \( \gamma \left( t\right)  = \left( {x, t}\right) ,\gamma \left( {t}_{0}\right)  \in \; \overline{B\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}, s}\right) } \) , and \( \left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right|  = {s}^{-2} \geq  {10}^{4}{r}_{ + }^{-2} \) . Hence by \( \Phi \) -pinching, \( R\left( {x, t}\right)  \geq  \frac{1}{100}{s}^{-2} \geq \; {100}{r}_{ + }^{-2} \) (cf. the remark just before the statement of Lemma 79.12). With reference to the constant \( \eta \) of (69.2), put \( \sigma  = {10}^{-6}\min \left( {1,\frac{1}{\eta }}\right) \) . Let \( \alpha  : \left\lbrack  {0,\widehat{\rho }}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \overline{B\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}, s}\right) } \subset  {\mathcal{M}}_{{t}_{0}}^{ - } \) be a minimizing geodesic from \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) to \( \gamma \left( {t}_{0}\right)  \in  \overline{B\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}, s}\right) } \) . We can find a point \( z \) along \( \alpha \) with \( {\operatorname{dist}}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {z,\gamma \left( {t}_{0}\right) }\right)  \leq  {\sigma s} \) and \( {\operatorname{dist}}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {z,{x}_{0}}\right)  \leq  \left( {1 - \sigma }\right) s \) . Let \( \bar{\gamma } : \left\lbrack  {t,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \mathcal{M} \) be the static curve ending at \( z \) and put \( \left( {\bar{x}, t}\right)  = \bar{\gamma }\left( t\right) \) . In brief, we get \( \left( {\bar{x}, t}\right) \) by "pulling \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) slightly inward from the boundary".

From the distance distortion estimate of Section 27, we can say that \( {\operatorname{dist}}_{t}\left( {\bar{x}, x}\right)  \leq  {10}^{6}{\sigma s} \) . Then applying (69.2) along a minimizing time- \( t \) curve from \( \bar{x} \) to \( x \) , we conclude that

(79.24)

\[
\left| {{R}^{-\frac{1}{2}}\left( {\bar{x}, t}\right)  - {R}^{-\frac{1}{2}}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  \frac{1}{2}\eta {\operatorname{dist}}_{t}\left( {\bar{x}, x}\right)  \leq  \frac{1}{2}s,
\]

so \( {R}^{-\frac{1}{2}}\left( {\bar{x}, t}\right)  \leq  {R}^{-\frac{1}{2}}\left( {x, t}\right)  + \frac{1}{2}s \leq  {20s} \) and hence \( R\left( {\bar{x}, t}\right)  \geq  \frac{1}{400}{s}^{-2} \geq  {25}{r}_{ + }^{-2} \) . In particular, \( \left( {\bar{x}, t}\right) \) has a canonical neighborhood. We also know that \( R\left( {\bar{x}, t}\right)  \leq  6\left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {\bar{x}, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  6{s}^{-2} \) . It follows from the definition of canonical neighborhoods (see Definition 69.1) that there is some universal constant so that \( \operatorname{vol}\left( {B\left( {\bar{x}, t,{10}^{-9}s}\right) }\right)  \geq \) const. \( {s}^{3} \) . (We recall that from Lemma 60.3, there is a \( \kappa  > 0 \) such that a standard solution is \( \kappa \) -noncollapsed as scales < 1.) The distance distortion estimate ensures that \( B\left( {\bar{x}, t,{10}^{-9}s}\right)  \subset  B\left( {z,{t}_{0},{10}^{-6}s}\right)  \subset \; B\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}, s}\right) \) . Then the standard volume distortion estimate implies that \( \operatorname{vol}\left( {B\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}, s}\right) }\right)  \geq \) const. \( \operatorname{vol}\left( {B\left( {\bar{x}, t,{10}^{-9}s}\right) }\right)  \geq \) const. \( {s}^{3} \) , again for some universal constant. Finally we use Bishop-Gromov volume comparison to get \( \operatorname{vol}\left( {B\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0},{r}_{0}}\right) }\right) {r}_{0}^{-3} \geq \) const. \( \operatorname{vol}\left( {B\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}, s}\right) }\right) {s}^{-3} \) .

In case (c) we apply (79.21), replacing the \( {r}_{0} \) parameter there by \( s \) , and Bishop-Gromov volume comparison as in case (b).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
(Justification of the canonical neighborhood assumption). Given any small \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) , there exist decreasing sequences \( 0 < {\widetilde{r}}_{j} < \varepsilon ,{\kappa }_{j} > 0 \) , and \( 0 < {\widetilde{\delta }}_{j} < {\varepsilon }^{2}, j = 1,2,\cdots \) , with the following property. Define the positive function \( \widetilde{\delta }\left( t\right) \) on \( \lbrack 0, + \infty ) \) by \( \widetilde{\delta }\left( t\right)  = {\widetilde{\delta }}_{j} \) for \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {\left( {j - 1}\right) {\varepsilon }^{2}, j{\varepsilon }^{2}}\right) \) . Suppose there is a surgically modified solution, defined on \( \lbrack 0, T) \) with \( T <  + \infty \) , to the Ricci flow which satisfies the following:

(1) it starts on a compact orientable three-manifold with normalized initial metric, and

(2) it has only a finite number of surgeries such that each surgery at a time \( t \in  \left( {0, T}\right) \) is a \( \delta \left( t\right) \) -cutoff surgery with

\[
0 < \delta \left( t\right)  \leq  \min \{ \widetilde{\delta }\left( t\right) ,\bar{\delta }\left( t\right) \} .
\]

Then on each time interval \( \left\lbrack  {\left( {j - 1}\right) {\varepsilon }^{2}, j{\varepsilon }^{2}}\right\rbrack  \bigcap \lbrack 0, T), j = 1,2,\cdots \) , the solution satisfies the \( {\kappa }_{j} \) -noncollapsing condition on all scales less than \( \varepsilon \) and the canonical neighborhood assumption (with accuracy \( \varepsilon \) ) with \( r = {\widetilde{r}}_{j} \) .

Here and in the following, we call a (three-dimensional) surgically modified solution \( {g}_{ij}\left( t\right) ,0 \leq  t < T,\kappa \) -noncollapsed at \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) on the scales less than \( \rho \) (for some \( \kappa  > 0,\rho  > 0 \) ) if it satisfies the following property: whenever \( r < \rho \) and

\[
\left| {{Rm}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  {r}^{-2}
\]

for all those \( \left( {x, t}\right)  \in  P\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}, r, - {r}^{2}}\right)  = \left\{  {\left( {{x}^{\prime },{t}^{\prime }}\right)  \mid  {x}^{\prime } \in  {B}_{{t}^{\prime }}\left( {{x}_{0}, r}\right) ,{t}^{\prime } \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0} - {r}^{2},{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack  }\right\} \) , for which the solution is defined, we have

\[
{\operatorname{Vol}}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0}, r}\right) }\right)  \geq  \kappa {r}^{3}.
\]

The proof of the proposition is by induction: having constructed our sequences for \( 1 \leq  j \leq  m \) , we make one more step, defining \( {\widetilde{r}}_{m + 1} \) , \( {\kappa }_{m + 1},{\widetilde{\delta }}_{m + 1} \) , and redefining \( {\widetilde{\delta }}_{m} = {\widetilde{\delta }}_{m + 1} \) . In view of the previous lemma, we only need to define \( {\widetilde{r}}_{m + 1} \) and \( {\widetilde{\delta }}_{m + 1} \) .

In Theorem 7.1.1 we have obtained the canonical neighborhood structure for smooth solutions. When adapting the arguments in the proof of Theorem 7.1.1 to the present surgical solutions, we will encounter the new difficulty of how to take a limit for the surgically modified solutions. The idea to overcome the difficulty consists of two parts. The first part, due to Perelman [104], is to choose \( {\widetilde{\delta }}_{m} \) and \( {\widetilde{\delta }}_{m + 1} \) small enough to push the surgical regions to infinity in space. (This is the reason why we need to redefine \( {\widetilde{\delta }}_{m} = {\widetilde{\delta }}_{m + 1} \) .) The second part is to show that solutions are smooth on some small, but uniform, time intervals (on compact subsets) so that we can apply Hamilton's compactness theorem, since we only have curvature bounds; otherwise Shi's interior derivative estimate may not be applicable. In fact, the second part is more crucial. That is just concerned with the question of whether the surgery times accumulate or not. Our argument will use the canonical neighborhood characterization of the standard solution in Lemma 7.3.5.

We now start to prove the proposition by contradiction. Suppose for sequence of positive numbers \( {r}^{\alpha } \) and \( {\widetilde{\delta }}^{\alpha \beta } \) , satisfying \( {r}^{\alpha } \rightarrow  0 \) as \( \alpha  \rightarrow  \infty \) and \( {\widetilde{\delta }}^{\alpha \beta } \leq  \frac{1}{\alpha  \cdot  \beta }\left( { \rightarrow  0}\right) \) , there exist sequences of solutions \( {g}_{ij}^{\alpha \beta } \) to the Ricci flow with surgery, where each of them has only a finite number of cutoff surgeries and has a compact orientable normalized three-manifold as initial data, so that the following two assertions hold:

(i) each \( \delta \) -cutoff at a time \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {\left( {m - 1}\right) {\varepsilon }^{2},\left( {m + 1}\right) {\varepsilon }^{2}}\right\rbrack \) satisfies \( \delta  \leq  {\widetilde{\delta }}^{\alpha \beta } \) ; and

(ii) the solutions satisfy the statement of the proposition on \( \left\lbrack  {0, m{\varepsilon }^{2}}\right\rbrack \) , but violate the canonical neighborhood assumption (with accuracy \( \varepsilon \) ) with \( r = {r}^{\alpha } \) on \( \left\lbrack  {m{\varepsilon }^{2},\left( {m + 1}\right) {\varepsilon }^{2}}\right\rbrack \) .

For each solution \( {g}_{ij}^{\alpha \beta } \) , we choose \( \bar{t} \) (depending on \( \alpha \) and \( \beta \) ) to be the nearly first time for which the canonical neighborhood assumption (with accuracy \( \varepsilon \) ) is violated. More precisely, we choose \( \bar{t} \in  \left\lbrack  {m{\varepsilon }^{2},\left( {m + 1}\right) {\varepsilon }^{2}}\right\rbrack \) so that the canonical neighborhood assumption with \( r = {r}^{\alpha } \) and with accuracy parameter \( \varepsilon \) is violated at some \( \left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right) \) , however the canonical neighborhood assumption with accuracy parameter \( {2\varepsilon } \) holds on \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {m{\varepsilon }^{2},\bar{t}}\right\rbrack \) . After passing to subsequences, we may assume each \( {\widetilde{\delta }}^{\alpha \beta } \) is less than the \( \widetilde{\delta } \) in Lemma 7.4.2 with \( r = {r}^{\alpha } \) when \( \alpha \) is fixed. Then by Lemma 7.4.2 we have uniform \( \kappa \) -noncollapsing on all scales less than \( \varepsilon \) on \( \left\lbrack  {0,\bar{t}}\right\rbrack \) with some \( \kappa  > 0 \) independent of \( \alpha ,\beta \) .

Slightly abusing notation, we will often drop the indices \( \alpha \) and \( \beta \) .

Let \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\alpha \beta } \) be the rescaled solutions around \( \left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right) \) with factors \( R\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right) \left( { \geq  {r}^{-2} \rightarrow   + \infty }\right) \) and shift the times \( \bar{t} \) to zero. We hope to take a limit of the rescaled solutions for subsequences of \( \alpha ,\beta  \rightarrow  \infty \) and show the limit is an orientable ancient \( \kappa \) -solution, which will give the desired contradiction. We divide our arguments into the following six steps.

Step 1. Let \( \left( {y,\widehat{t}}\right) \) be a point on the rescaled solution \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\alpha \beta } \) with \( \widetilde{R}\left( {y,\widehat{t}}\right)  \leq  A \) (for some \( A \geq  1 \) ) and \( \widehat{t} \in  \left\lbrack  {-\left( {\bar{t} - \left( {m - 1}\right) {\varepsilon }^{2}}\right) R\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right) ,0}\right\rbrack \) . Then we have estimate

(7.4.14)

\[
\widetilde{R}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  {10A}
\]

for those \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) in the parabolic neighborhood \( P\left( {y,\widehat{t},\frac{1}{2}{\eta }^{-1}{A}^{-\frac{1}{2}}, - \frac{1}{8}{\eta }^{-1}{A}^{-1}}\right)  \triangleq \; \left\{  {\left( {{x}^{\prime },{t}^{\prime }}\right)  \mid  {x}^{\prime } \in  {\widetilde{B}}_{{t}^{\prime }}\left( {y,\frac{1}{2}{\eta }^{-1}{A}^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) ,{t}^{\prime } \in  \left\lbrack  {\widehat{t} - \frac{1}{8}{\eta }^{-1}{A}^{-1},\widehat{t}}\right\rbrack  }\right\} \) , for which the rescaled solution is defined.

Indeed, as in the first step of the proof of Theorem 7.1.1, this follows directly from the gradient estimates (7.3.4) in the canonical neighborhood assumption with parameter \( {2\varepsilon } \) .

Step 2. In this step, we will prove three time extension results.

Assertion 1. For arbitrarily fixed \( \alpha ,0 < A <  + \infty ,1 \leq  C <  + \infty \) and \( 0 \leq  B < \frac{1}{2}{\varepsilon }^{2}{\left( {r}^{\alpha }\right) }^{-2} - \frac{1}{8}{\eta }^{-1}{C}^{-1} \) , there is a \( {\beta }_{0} = {\beta }_{0}\left( {\varepsilon , A, B, C}\right) \) (independent of \( \alpha \) ) such that if \( \beta  \geq  {\beta }_{0} \) and the rescaled solution \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\alpha \beta } \) on the ball \( {\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x}, A}\right) \) is defined on a time interval \( \left\lbrack  {-b,0}\right\rbrack \) with \( 0 \leq  b \leq  B \) and the scalar curvature satisfies

\[
\widetilde{R}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  C,\;\text{ on }{\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x}, A}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {-b,0}\right\rbrack  ,
\]

then the rescaled solution \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\alpha \beta } \) on the ball \( {\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x}, A}\right) \) is also defined on the extended time interval \( \left\lbrack  {-b - \frac{1}{8}{\eta }^{-1}{C}^{-1},0}\right\rbrack \) .

Before giving the proof, we make a simple observation: once a space point in the Ricci flow with surgery is removed by surgery at some time, then it never appears for later time; if a space point at some time \( t \) cannot be defined before the time \( t \) , then either the point lies in a gluing cap of the surgery at time \( t \) or the time \( t \) is the initial time of the Ricci flow.

Proof of Assertion 1. Firstly we claim that there exists \( {\beta }_{0} = {\beta }_{0}\left( {\varepsilon , A, B, C}\right) \) such that when \( \beta  \geq  {\beta }_{0} \) , the rescaled solution \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\alpha \beta } \) on the ball \( {\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x}, A}\right) \) can be defined before the time \( - b \) (i.e., there are no surgeries interfering in \( {\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x}, A}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {-b - {\epsilon }^{\prime }, - b}\right\rbrack \) for some \( \left. {{\epsilon }^{\prime } > 0}\right) \) .

We argue by contradiction. Suppose not, then there is some point \( \widetilde{x} \in  {\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x}, A}\right) \) such that the rescaled solution \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\alpha \beta } \) at \( \widetilde{x} \) cannot be defined before the time \( - b \) . By the above observation, there is a surgery at the time \( - b \) such that the point \( \widetilde{x} \) lies in the instant gluing cap.

Let \( \widetilde{h}\left( { = R{\left( \bar{x},\bar{t}\right) }^{\frac{1}{2}}h}\right) \) be the cut-off radius at the time \( - b \) for the rescaled solution. Clearly, there is a universal constant \( D \) such that \( {D}^{-1}\widetilde{h} \leq  \widetilde{R}{\left( \widetilde{x}, - b\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}} \leq  D\widetilde{h} \) .

By Lemma 7.3.4 and looking at the rescaled solution at the time \( - b \) , the gluing cap and the adjacent \( \delta \) -neck, of radius \( \widetilde{h} \) , constitute a \( {\left( {\widetilde{\delta }}^{\alpha \beta }\right) }^{\frac{1}{2}} \) -cap \( \mathcal{K} \) . For any fixed small positive constant \( {\delta }^{\prime } \) (much smaller than \( \varepsilon \) ), we see that

\[
{\widetilde{B}}_{\left( -b\right) }\left( {\widetilde{x},{\left( {\delta }^{\prime }\right) }^{-1}\widetilde{R}{\left( \widetilde{x}, - b\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right)  \subset  \mathcal{K}
\]

when \( \beta \) large enough. We first verify the following

CLAIM 1. For any small constants \( 0 < \widetilde{\theta } < 1,{\delta }^{\prime } > 0 \) , there exists a \( \beta \left( {{\delta }^{\prime },\varepsilon ,\widetilde{\theta }}\right)  > 0 \) such that when \( \beta  \geq  \beta \left( {{\delta }^{\prime },\varepsilon ,\widetilde{\theta }}\right) \) , we have

(i) the rescaled solution \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\alpha \beta } \) over \( {\widetilde{B}}_{\left( -b\right) }\left( {\widetilde{x},{\left( {\delta }^{\prime }\right) }^{-1}\widetilde{h}}\right) \) is defined on the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {-b,0}\right\rbrack   \cap  \left\lbrack  {-b, - b + \left( {1 - \widetilde{\theta }}\right) {\widetilde{h}}^{2}}\right\rbrack \)

(ii) the ball \( {\widetilde{B}}_{\left( -b\right) }\left( {\widetilde{x},{\left( {\delta }^{\prime }\right) }^{-1}\widetilde{h}}\right) \) in the \( {\left( {\widetilde{\delta }}^{\alpha \beta }\right) }^{\frac{1}{2}} \) -cap \( \mathcal{K} \) evolved by the Ricci flow on the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {-b,0}\right\rbrack   \cap  \left\lbrack  {-b, - b + \left( {1 - \widetilde{\theta }}\right) {\widetilde{h}}^{2}}\right\rbrack \) is, after scaling with factor \( {\widetilde{h}}^{-2} \) , \( {\delta }^{\prime } \) -close (in the \( {C}^{\left\lbrack  {\delta }^{\prime  - 1}\right\rbrack  } \) topology) to the corresponding subset of the standard solution.

This claim essentially follows from Lemma 7.3.6. Indeed, suppose there is a surgery at some time \( \widetilde{\widetilde{t}} \in  \left\lbrack  {-b,0}\right\rbrack   \cap  \left( {-b, - b + \left( {1 - \widetilde{\theta }}\right) {\widetilde{h}}^{2}}\right\rbrack \) which removes some point \( \widetilde{\widetilde{x}} \in  {\widetilde{B}}_{\left( -b\right) }\left( {\widetilde{x},{\left( {\delta }^{\prime }\right) }^{-1}\widetilde{h}}\right) \) . We assume \( \widetilde{\widetilde{t}} \in  ( - b,0\rbrack \) is the first time with that property.

Then by Lemma 7.3.6, there is a \( \bar{\delta } = \bar{\delta }\left( {{\delta }^{\prime },\varepsilon ,\widetilde{\theta }}\right) \) such that if \( {\widetilde{\delta }}^{\alpha \beta } < \bar{\delta } \) , then the ball \( {\widetilde{B}}_{\left( -b\right) }\left( {\widetilde{x},{\left( {\delta }^{\prime }\right) }^{-1}\widetilde{h}}\right) \) in the \( {\left( {\widetilde{\delta }}^{\alpha \beta }\right) }^{\frac{1}{2}} \) -cap \( \mathcal{K} \) evolved by the Ricci flow on the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {-b,\widetilde{\widetilde{t}}}\right) \) is, after scaling with factor \( {\widetilde{h}}^{-2},{\delta }^{\prime } \) -close to the corresponding subset of the standard solution. Note that the metrics for times in \( \lbrack  - b,\widetilde{\widetilde{t}}) \) on \( {\widetilde{B}}_{\left( -b\right) }\left( {\widetilde{x},{\left( {\delta }^{\prime }\right) }^{-1}\widetilde{h}}\right) \) are equivalent. By Lemma 7.3.6, the solution on \( {\widetilde{B}}_{\left( -b\right) }\left( {\widetilde{x},{\left( {\delta }^{\prime }\right) }^{-1}\widetilde{h}}\right) \) keeps looking like a cap for \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {-b,\widetilde{\widetilde{t}}}\right\rbrack \) . On the other hand, by the definition, the surgery is always done along the middle two-sphere of a \( \delta \) -neck with \( \delta  < {\widetilde{\delta }}^{\alpha \beta } \) . Then for \( \beta \) large, all the points in \( {\widetilde{B}}_{\left( -b\right) }\left( {\widetilde{x},{\left( {\delta }^{\prime }\right) }^{-1}\widetilde{h}}\right) \) are removed (as a part of a capped horn) at the time \( \widetilde{\widetilde{t}} \) . But \( \widetilde{x} \) (near the tip of the cap) exists past the time \( \widetilde{\widetilde{t}} \) . This is a contradiction. Hence we have proved that \( {\widetilde{B}}_{\left( -b\right) }\left( {\widetilde{x},{\left( {\delta }^{\prime }\right) }^{-1}\widetilde{h}}\right) \) is defined on the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {-b,0}\right\rbrack   \cap  \left\lbrack  {-b, - b + \left( {1 - \widetilde{\theta }}\right) {\widetilde{h}}^{2}}\right\rbrack \) .

The \( {\delta }^{\prime } \) -closeness of the solution on \( {\widetilde{B}}_{\left( -b\right) }\left( {\widetilde{x},{\left( {\delta }^{\prime }\right) }^{-1}h}\right)  \times  \left( {\left\lbrack  {-b,0}\right\rbrack   \cap  \left\lbrack  {-b, - b + \left( {1 - \widetilde{\theta }}\right) {\widetilde{h}}^{2}}\right\rbrack  }\right) \) with the corresponding subset of the standard solution follows from Lemma 7.3.6. Then we have proved Claim 1.

We next verify the following

CLAIM 2. There is \( \widetilde{\theta } = \widetilde{\theta }\left( {CB}\right) ,0 < \widetilde{\theta } < 1 \) , such that \( b \leq  \left( {1 - \widetilde{\theta }}\right) {\widetilde{h}}^{2} \) when \( \beta \) large.

Note from Proposition 7.3.3, there is a universal constant \( {D}^{\prime } > 0 \) such that the standard solution satisfies the following curvature estimate

\[
R\left( {y, s}\right)  \geq  \frac{2{D}^{\prime }}{1 - s}.
\]

We choose \( \widetilde{\theta } = {D}^{\prime }/2\left( {{D}^{\prime } + {CB}}\right) \) . Then for \( \beta \) large enough, the rescaled solution satisfies

(7.4.15)

\[
\widetilde{R}\left( {x, t}\right)  \geq  \frac{{D}^{\prime }}{1 - \left( {t + b}\right) {\widetilde{h}}^{-2}}{\widetilde{h}}^{-2}
\]

on \( {\widetilde{B}}_{\left( -b\right) }\left( {\widetilde{x},{\left( {\delta }^{\prime }\right) }^{-1}\widetilde{h}}\right)  \times  \left( {\left\lbrack  {-b,0}\right\rbrack   \cap  \left\lbrack  {-b, - b + \left( {1 - \widetilde{\theta }}\right) {\widetilde{h}}^{2}}\right\rbrack  }\right) \) .

Suppose \( b \geq  \left( {1 - \widetilde{\theta }}\right) {\widetilde{h}}^{2} \) . Then by combining with the assumption \( \widetilde{R}\left( {\widetilde{x}, t}\right)  \leq  C \) for \( t = \left( {1 - \widetilde{\theta }}\right) {\widetilde{h}}^{2} - b \) , we have

\[
C \geq  \frac{{D}^{\prime }}{1 - \left( {t + b}\right) {\widetilde{h}}^{-2}}{\widetilde{h}}^{-2},
\]

and then

\[
1 \geq  \left( {1 - \widetilde{\theta }}\right) \left( {1 + \frac{{D}^{\prime }}{CB}}\right) .
\]

This is a contradiction. Hence we have proved Claim 2.

The combination of the above two claims shows that there is a positive constant \( 0 < \widetilde{\theta } = \widetilde{\theta }\left( {CB}\right)  < 1 \) such that for any small \( {\delta }^{\prime } > 0 \) , there is a positive \( \beta \left( {{\delta }^{\prime },\varepsilon ,\widetilde{\theta }}\right) \) such that when \( \beta  \geq  \beta \left( {{\delta }^{\prime },\varepsilon ,\widetilde{\theta }}\right) \) , we have \( b \leq  \left( {1 - \widetilde{\theta }}\right) {\widetilde{h}}^{2} \) and the rescaled solution in the ball \( {\widetilde{B}}_{\left( -b\right) }\left( {\widetilde{x},{\left( {\delta }^{\prime }\right) }^{-1}\widetilde{h}}\right) \) on the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {-b,0}\right\rbrack \) is, after scaling with factor \( {\widetilde{h}}^{-2},{\delta }^{\prime } \) -close (in the \( {C}^{\left\lbrack  {\left( {\delta }^{\prime }\right) }^{-1}\right\rbrack  } \) topology) to the corresponding subset of the standard solution.

By (7.4.15) and the assumption \( \widetilde{R} \leq  C \) on \( {\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x}, A}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {-b,0}\right\rbrack \) , we know that the cut-off radius \( \widetilde{h} \) at the time \( - b \) for the rescaled solution satisfies

\[
\widetilde{h} \geq  \sqrt{\frac{{D}^{\prime }}{C}}.
\]

Let \( {\delta }^{\prime } > 0 \) be much smaller than \( \varepsilon \) and \( \min \left\{  {{A}^{-1}, A}\right\} \) . Since \( {\widetilde{d}}_{0}\left( {\widetilde{x},\bar{x}}\right)  \leq  A \) , it follows that there is constant \( C\left( \widetilde{\theta }\right) \) depending only on \( \widetilde{\theta } \) such that \( {\widetilde{d}}_{\left( -b\right) }\left( {\widetilde{x},\bar{x}}\right)  \leq  C\left( \widetilde{\theta }\right) A \ll \; {\left( {\delta }^{\prime }\right) }^{-1}\widetilde{h} \) . We now apply Lemma 7.3.5 with the accuracy parameter \( \varepsilon /2 \) . Let \( C\left( {\varepsilon /2}\right) \) be the positive constant in Lemma 7.3.5. Without loss of generality, we may assume the positive constant \( {C}_{1}\left( \varepsilon \right) \) in the canonical neighborhood assumption is larger than \( {4C}\left( {\varepsilon /2}\right) \) . When \( {\delta }^{\prime }\left( { > 0}\right) \) is much smaller than \( \varepsilon \) and \( \min \left\{  {{A}^{-1}, A}\right\} \) , the point \( \bar{x} \) at the time \( \bar{t} \) has a neighborhood which is either a \( \frac{3}{4}\varepsilon \) -cap or a \( \frac{3}{4}\varepsilon \) -neck.

Since the canonical neighborhood assumption with accuracy parameter \( \varepsilon \) is violated at \( \left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right) \) , the neighborhood of the point \( \bar{x} \) at the new time zero for the rescaled solution must be a \( \frac{3}{4}\varepsilon \) -neck. By Lemma 7.3.5 (b), we know the neighborhood is the slice at the time zero of the parabolic neighborhood

\[
P\left( {\bar{x},0,\frac{4}{3}{\varepsilon }^{-1}\widetilde{R}{\left( \bar{x},0\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}, - \min \left\{  {\widetilde{R}{\left( \bar{x},0\right) }^{-1}, b}\right\}  }\right)
\]

(with \( \widetilde{R}\left( {\bar{x},0}\right)  = 1 \) ) which is \( \frac{3}{4}\varepsilon \) -close (in the \( {C}^{\left\lbrack  \frac{4}{3}{\varepsilon }^{-1}\right\rbrack  } \) topology) to the corresponding subset of the evolving standard cylinder \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \times  \mathbb{R} \) over the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {-\min \{ b,1\} ,0}\right\rbrack \) with scalar curvature 1 at the time zero. If \( b \geq  1 \) , the \( \frac{3}{4}\varepsilon \) -neck is strong, which is a contradiction. While if \( b < 1 \) , the \( \frac{3}{4}\varepsilon \) -neck at time \( - b \) is contained in the union of the gluing cap and the adjacent \( \delta \) -neck where the \( \delta \) -cutoff surgery took place. Since \( \varepsilon \) is small (say \( \varepsilon  < 1/{100} \) ), it is clear that the point \( \bar{x} \) at time \( - b \) is the center of an \( \varepsilon \) -neck which is entirely contained in the adjacent \( \delta \) -neck. By the proof of Lemma 7.3.2, the adjacent \( \delta \) -neck approximates an ancient \( \kappa \) -solution. This implies the point \( \bar{x} \) at the time \( \bar{t} \) has a strong \( \varepsilon \) -neck, which is also a contradiction.

Hence we have proved that there exists \( {\beta }_{0} = {\beta }_{0}\left( {\varepsilon , A, B, C}\right) \) such that when \( \beta  \geq  {\beta }_{0} \) , the rescaled solution on the ball \( {\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x}, A}\right) \) can be defined before the time \( - b \) .

Let \( \left\lbrack  {{t}_{A}^{\alpha \beta },0}\right\rbrack   \supset  \left\lbrack  {-b,0}\right\rbrack \) be the largest time interval so that the rescaled solution \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\alpha \beta } \) can be defined on \( {\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x}, A}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{A}^{\alpha \beta },0}\right\rbrack \) . We finally claim that \( {t}_{A}^{\alpha \beta } \leq   - b - \frac{1}{8}{\eta }^{-1}{C}^{-1} \) for \( \beta \) large enough.

Indeed, suppose not, by the gradient estimates as in Step 1, we have the curvature estimate

\[
\widetilde{R}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  {10C}
\]

on \( {\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x}, A}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{A}^{\alpha \beta }, - b}\right\rbrack \) . Hence we have the curvature estimate

\[
\widetilde{R}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  {10C}

on \( {\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x}, A}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{A}^{\alpha \beta },0}\right\rbrack \) . We need to show \( - {t}_{\max } =  - \infty \) . Suppose \( - {t}_{\max } >  - \infty \) , there are only the following two possibilities: either

(1) The curvature of the limiting solution \( \left( {{M}_{\infty },{\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\infty }\left( {\cdot , t}\right) }\right) \) becomes unbounded as \( t \searrow   - {t}_{\max } \) ; or

(2) For each small constant \( \theta  > 0 \) and each large integer \( {k}_{0} > 0 \) , there is some \( k \geq \; {k}_{0} \) such that the rescaled solution \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{k}{\beta }_{k}} \) has a surgery time \( {T}_{k} \in  \left\lbrack  {-{t}_{\max } - \theta ,0}\right\rbrack \) and a surgery point \( {x}_{k} \) lying in a gluing cap at the times \( {T}_{k} \) so that \( {d}_{{T}_{k}}^{2}\left( {{x}_{k},\bar{x}}\right) \) is uniformly bounded from above by a constant independent of \( \theta \) and \( {k}_{0} \) .

We next claim that the possibility (1) always occurs. Suppose not; then the curvature of the limiting solution \( \left( {{M}_{\infty },{\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\infty }\left( {\cdot , t}\right) }\right) \) is bounded on \( {M}_{\infty } \times  \left( {-{t}_{\max },0}\right\rbrack \) by some positive constant \( \widehat{C} \) . In particular, for any \( A > 0 \) , there is a sufficiently large integer \( {k}_{1} > 0 \) such that any rescaled solution \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{k}{\beta }_{k}} \) with \( k \geq  {k}_{1} \) on the geodesic ball \( {\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x}, A}\right) \) is defined on the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {-{t}_{\max } + \frac{1}{50}{\eta }^{-1}{\widehat{C}}^{-1},0}\right\rbrack \) and its scalar curvature is bounded by \( 2\widehat{C} \) there. (Here, without loss of generality, we may assume that the upper bound \( \widehat{C} \) is so large that \( - {t}_{\max } + \frac{1}{50}{\eta }^{-1}{\widehat{C}}^{-1} < 0 \) .) By Assertion 1 in Step 2, for \( k \) large enough, the rescaled solution \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{k}{\beta }_{k}} \) over \( {\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x}, A}\right) \) can be defined on the extended time interval \( \left\lbrack  {-{t}_{\max } - \frac{1}{50}{\eta }^{-1}{\widehat{C}}^{-1},0}\right\rbrack \) and has the scalar curvature \( \widetilde{R} \leq  {10}\widehat{C} \) on \( {\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x}, A}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {-{t}_{\max } - \frac{1}{50}{\eta }^{-1}{\widehat{C}}^{-1},0}\right\rbrack \) . So we can extract a smooth limit from the sequence to get the limiting solution which is defined on a larger time interval \( \left\lbrack  {-{t}_{\max } - \frac{1}{50}{\eta }^{-1}{\widehat{C}}^{-1},0}\right\rbrack \) . This contradicts the definition of the maximal time \( - {t}_{\max } \) .

It remains to exclude the possibility (1).

By using Li-Yau-Hamilton inequality (Corollary 2.5.5) again, we have

\[
{\widetilde{R}}_{\infty }\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  \frac{{t}_{\max }}{t + {t}_{\max }}\widetilde{Q}.
\]

So we only need to control the curvature near \( - {t}_{\max } \) . Exactly as in Step 4 in the proof of Theorem 7.1.1, it follows from Li-Yau-Hamilton inequality that

(7.4.16)

\[
{\widetilde{d}}_{0}\left( {x, y}\right)  \leq  {\widetilde{d}}_{t}\left( {x, y}\right)  \leq  {\widetilde{d}}_{0}\left( {x, y}\right)  + {30}{t}_{\max }\sqrt{\widetilde{Q}}
\]

for any \( x, y \in  {M}_{\infty } \) and \( t \in  \left( {-{t}_{\max },0}\right\rbrack \) .

Since the infimum of the scalar curvature is nondecreasing in time, we have some point \( {y}_{\infty } \in  {M}_{\infty } \) and some time \( - {t}_{\max } < {t}_{\infty } <  - {t}_{\max } + \frac{1}{50}{\eta }^{-1} \) such that \( {\widetilde{R}}_{\infty }\left( {{y}_{\infty },{t}_{\infty }}\right)  < \; 5/4 \) . By (7.4.16), there is a constant \( {\widetilde{A}}_{0} > 0 \) such that \( {\widetilde{d}}_{t}\left( {\bar{x},{y}_{\infty }}\right)  \leq  {\widetilde{A}}_{0}/2 \) for all \( t \in  \left( {-{t}_{\max },0}\right\rbrack \) .

Now we come back to the rescaled solution \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{k}{\beta }_{k}} \) . Clearly, for arbitrarily given small \( {\epsilon }^{\prime } > 0 \) , when \( k \) large enough, there is a point \( {y}_{k} \) in the underlying manifold of \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{k}{\beta }_{k}} \) at time 0 satisfying the following properties

(7.4.17)

\[
\widetilde{R}\left( {{y}_{k},{t}_{\infty }}\right)  < \frac{3}{2},\;{\widetilde{d}}_{t}\left( {\bar{x},{y}_{k}}\right)  \leq  {\widetilde{A}}_{0}
\]

for \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {-{t}_{\max } + {\epsilon }^{\prime },0}\right\rbrack \) . By the definition of convergence, we know that for any fixed \( {A}_{0} \geq  2{\widetilde{A}}_{0} \) , for \( k \) large enough, the rescaled solution over \( {\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x},{A}_{0}}\right) \) is defined on the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {{t}_{\infty },0}\right\rbrack \) and satisfies

\[
\widetilde{R}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  \frac{2{t}_{\max }}{t + {t}_{\max }}\widetilde{Q}
\]

on \( {\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x},{A}_{0}}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{\infty },0}\right\rbrack \) . Then by Assertion 2 of Step 2, we have proved that there is a sufficiently large integer \( {\bar{k}}_{0} \) such that when \( k \geq  {\bar{k}}_{0} \) , the rescaled solutions \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{k}{\beta }_{k}} \) at \( {y}_{k} \) can be defined on \( \left\lbrack  {-{t}_{\max } - \frac{1}{50}{\eta }^{-1},0}\right\rbrack \) , and satisfy

\[
\widetilde{R}\left( {{y}_{k}, t}\right)  \leq  {15}
\]

for \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {-{t}_{\max } - \frac{1}{50}{\eta }^{-1},{t}_{\infty }}\right\rbrack \) .

We now prove a statement analogous to Assertion 4 (i) of Step 3.

Assertion 5. For the above rescaled solutions \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{k}{\beta }_{k}} \) and \( {\bar{k}}_{0} \) , we have that for any \( L > 0 \) , there is a positive constant \( \omega \left( L\right) \) such that the rescaled solutions \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{k}{\beta }_{k}} \) satisfy

\[
\widetilde{R}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  \omega \left( L\right)
\]

for all \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) with \( {\widetilde{d}}_{t}\left( {x,{y}_{k}}\right)  \leq  L \) and \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {-{t}_{\max } - \frac{1}{50}{\eta }^{-1},{t}_{\infty }}\right\rbrack \) , and for all \( k \geq  {\bar{k}}_{0} \) .

Proof of Assertion 5. We slightly modify the argument in the proof of Assertion 4 (i). Let

\[
M\left( \rho \right)  = \sup \left\{  {\widetilde{R}\left( {x, t}\right)  \mid  {\widetilde{d}}_{t}\left( {x,{y}_{k}}\right)  \leq  \rho }\right. \text{ and }t \in  \left\lbrack  {-{t}_{\max } - \frac{1}{50}{\eta }^{-1},{t}_{\infty }}\right\rbrack
\]

\[
\text{ in the rescaled solutions }\left. {{\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{k}{\beta }_{k}}, k \geq  {\bar{k}}_{0}}\right\}
\]

and

\[
{\rho }_{0} = \sup \{ \rho  > 0 \mid  M\left( \rho \right)  <  + \infty \} .
\]

Note that the estimate (7.4.14) implies that \( {\rho }_{0} > 0 \) . We only need to show \( {\rho }_{0} =  + \infty \) .

We argue by contradiction. Suppose \( {\rho }_{0} <  + \infty \) . Then, after passing to a subsequence, there is a sequence \( \left( {{\widetilde{y}}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) \) in the rescaled solutions \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{k}{\beta }_{k}} \) with \( {t}_{k} \in  \left\lbrack  {-{t}_{\max } - \frac{1}{50}{\eta }^{-1},{t}_{\infty }}\right\rbrack \) and \( {\widetilde{d}}_{{t}_{k}}\left( {{y}_{k},{\widetilde{y}}_{k}}\right)  \rightarrow  {\rho }_{0} <  + \infty \) such that \( \widetilde{R}\left( {{\widetilde{y}}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right)  \rightarrow   + \infty \) . Denote by \( {\gamma }_{k} \) a minimizing geodesic segment from \( {y}_{k} \) to \( {\widetilde{y}}_{k} \) at the time \( {t}_{k} \) and denote by \( {\widetilde{B}}_{{t}_{k}}\left( {{y}_{k},{\rho }_{0}}\right) \) the open geodesic ball centered at \( {y}_{k} \) of radius \( {\rho }_{0} \) on the rescaled solution \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{k}{\beta }_{k}}\left( {\cdot ,{t}_{k}}\right) \) .

For any \( 0 < \rho  < {\rho }_{0} \) with \( \rho \) near \( {\rho }_{0} \) , by applying Assertion 3 as before, we get that the rescaled solutions on the balls \( {B}_{{t}_{k}}\left( {{y}_{k},\rho }\right) \) are defined on the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {{t}_{k} - \frac{1}{16}{\eta }^{-1}M{\left( \rho \right) }^{-1},{t}_{k}}\right\rbrack \) for all large \( k \) . By Step 1 and Shi’s derivative estimate, we further know that the covariant derivatives and higher order derivatives of the curvatures on \( {\widetilde{B}}_{{t}_{k}}\left( {{y}_{k},\rho  - \frac{\left( {\rho }_{0} - \rho \right) }{2}}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{k} - \frac{1}{32}{\eta }^{-1}M{\left( \rho \right) }^{-1},{t}_{k}}\right\rbrack \) are also uniformly bounded. Then by the uniform \( \kappa \) -noncollapsing property and Hamilton’s compactness theorem (Theorem 4.1.5), after passing to a subsequence, we can assume that the marked sequence \( \left( {{\widetilde{B}}_{{t}_{k}}\left( {{y}_{k},{\rho }_{0}}\right) ,{\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{k}{\beta }_{k}}\left( {\cdot ,{t}_{k}}\right) ,{y}_{k}}\right) \) converges in the \( {C}_{loc}^{\infty } \) topology to a marked (noncomplete) manifold \( \left( {{B}_{\infty },{\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\infty },{y}_{\infty }}\right) \) and the geodesic segments \( {\gamma }_{k} \) converge to a geodesic segment (missing an endpoint) \( {\gamma }_{\infty } \subset  {B}_{\infty } \) emanating from \( {y}_{\infty } \) .

Clearly, the limit also has nonnegative sectional curvature by the pinching assumption. Then by repeating the same argument as in the proof of Assertion 4 (i) in the rest, we derive a contradiction with Hamilton's strong maximum principle. This proves Assertion 5.

We then apply the second estimate of (7.4.17) and Assertion 5 to conclude that for any large constant \( 0 < A <  + \infty \) , there is a positive constant \( C\left( A\right) \) such that for any small \( {\epsilon }^{\prime } > 0 \) , the rescaled solutions \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{k}{\beta }_{k}} \) satisfy

(7.4.18)

\[
\widetilde{R}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  C\left( A\right)
\]

for all \( x \in  {\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x}, A}\right) \) and \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {-{t}_{\max } + {\epsilon }^{\prime },0}\right\rbrack \) , and for all sufficiently large \( k \) . Then by applying Assertion 1 in Step 2, we conclude that the rescaled solutions \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{k}{\beta }_{k}} \) on the geodesic balls \( {\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x}, A}\right) \) are also defined on the extended time interval \( \left\lbrack  {-{t}_{\max } + {\epsilon }^{\prime } - }\right. \; \left. {\frac{1}{8}{\eta }^{-1}C{\left( A\right) }^{-1},0}\right\rbrack \) for all sufficiently large \( k \) . Furthermore, by the gradient estimates as in Step 1, we have

\[
\widetilde{R}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  {10C}\left( A\right)
\]

for \( x \in  {\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x}, A}\right) \) and \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {-{t}_{\max } + {\epsilon }^{\prime } - \frac{1}{8}{\eta }^{-1}C{\left( A\right) }^{-1},0}\right\rbrack \) . Since \( {\epsilon }^{\prime } > 0 \) is arbitrarily small and the positive constant \( C\left( A\right) \) is independent of \( {\epsilon }^{\prime } \) , we conclude that the rescaled solutions \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{k}{\beta }_{k}} \) on \( {\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x}, A}\right) \) are defined on the extended time interval \( \left\lbrack  {-{t}_{\max } - }\right. \; \left. {\frac{1}{16}{\eta }^{-1}C{\left( A\right) }^{-1},0}\right\rbrack \) and satisfy

(7.4.19)

\[
\widetilde{R}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  {10C}\left( A\right) ,
\]

for \( x \in  {\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x}, A}\right) \) and \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {-{t}_{\max } - \frac{1}{16}{\eta }^{-1}C{\left( A\right) }^{-1},0}\right\rbrack \) , and for all sufficiently large \( k \) .

Now, by taking convergent subsequences from the rescaled solutions \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{k}{\beta }_{k}} \) , we see that the limit solution is defined smoothly on a space-time open subset of \( {M}_{\infty } \times \; ( - \infty ,0\rbrack \) containing \( {M}_{\infty } \times  \left\lbrack  {-{t}_{\max },0}\right\rbrack \) . By Step 4, we see that the limiting metric \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\infty }\left( {\cdot , - {t}_{\max }}\right) \) at time \( - {t}_{\max } \) has bounded curvature. Then by combining with the canonical neighborhood assumption of accuracy \( {2\varepsilon } \) , we conclude that the curvature of the limit is uniformly bounded on the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {-{t}_{\max },0}\right\rbrack \) . So we have excluded the possibility (1).

Hence we have proved a subsequence of the rescaled solutions converges to an orientable ancient \( \kappa \) -solution.

Finally by combining with the canonical neighborhood theorem (Theorem 6.4.6), we see that \( \left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right) \) has a canonical neighborhood with parameter \( \varepsilon \) , which is a contradiction. Therefore we have completed the proof of the proposition. 0

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For any \( C < \infty \) the following holds. Suppose that \( X \) is a connected subset of a Riemannian three-manifold \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) . Suppose that every point of \( X \) is either the center of an \( \epsilon \) -neck or is contained in the core of a \( \left( {C,\epsilon }\right) \) -cap. Then one of the following holds (see FIG. 4):

(1) \( X \) is contained in a component of \( M \) that is the union of two \( \left( {C,\epsilon }\right) \) -caps and is diffeomorphic to one of \( {S}^{3},\mathbb{R}{P}^{3} \) or \( \mathbb{R}{P}^{3}\# \mathbb{R}{P}^{3} \) .

(2) \( X \) is contained in a component of \( M \) that is a double \( C \) -capped \( \epsilon \) -tube. This component is diffeomorphic to \( {S}^{3},\mathbb{R}{P}^{3} \) or \( \mathbb{R}{P}^{3}\# \mathbb{R}{P}^{3} \) .

(3) \( X \) is contained in a single \( \left( {C,\epsilon }\right) \) -cap.

(4) \( X \) is contained in a \( C \) -capped \( \epsilon \) -tube.

(5) \( X \) is contained in an \( \epsilon \) -tube.

(6) \( X \) is contained in a component of \( M \) that is an \( \epsilon \) -fibration, which itself is a union of \( \epsilon \) -necks.
